title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 161 (Bailee's responsibility when goods are not duly returned)

content.overview: Section 161 provides that if, by the default of the bailee, the goods are not returned, delivered or tendered at the proper time, he is responsible to the bailor for any loss, destruction or deterioration of the goods from that time.
content.glance: If the bailee defaults in returning, delivering or tendering the goods at the proper time, he is responsible for any subsequent loss, destruction or deterioration.
content.study: If, by the default of the bailee, the goods are not returned, delivered or tendered at the proper time, he is responsible to the bailor for any loss, destruction or deterioration of the goods from that time. Current-law framing: default triggers liability from the proper time onward for subsequent loss etc.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If, by the default of the bailee, the goods are not returned, delivered or tendered at the proper time, he is responsible to the bailor for any loss, destruction or deterioration of the goods from that time.

examples.title: Default in timely return
examples.body: Bailee fails to return goods at the proper time. Goods are later destroyed. Bailee is responsible for the loss from the proper time under Section 161.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee defaults in returning the goods at the proper time and they are subsequently lost. Is he liable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 161 makes him responsible for any loss, destruction or deterioration from that time.
